originalFamilyScopeSummary: Add market category pills to Extension's Perps tab for direct category filtering
currentTriggerSummary: pr-complete: feat(perps): add Products section to the Perps tab and category pills to the market list
notes: TAT-3848's four acceptance criteria are all met on the branch head, with two deliberately reinterpreted by review. (1) Category pills on the Perps tab: the Products section renders one MMDS ButtonFilter chip per controller category — live capture at artifacts/probe2/screenshots/perps-tab.png shows Crypto, Stocks, Pre-IPO, Indices, ETFs, Commodities, Forex, New. The ticket asked for a horizontally-scrollable row; geositta's CHANGES_REQUESTED review (5096562114) rejected horizontal scroll as a mobile gesture pattern hostile to mouse and keyboard users on web, so the chips wrap instead. That is a reviewer-directed change of means, not a reduction of scope — every category is still on screen, and more reachable than the ticket's own design. (2) Tapping a pill opens the market list pre-filtered: proved live, recipe node fix2-assert-crypto-pressed, with artifacts/recipe-run/screenshots/market-list-filtered.png showing the Crypto pill pressed and 178 markets. (3) Skeleton-gated with no layout jump: the rail reserves a pill per category while loading, and this round added the watchlist slot above Products that review found missing — unit-proved by recipe node fix4. (4) Keyboard/focus navigable: chips are native ButtonFilter buttons in a role="group", Tab-reachable in order, which is what dropped the original overflow menu's keyboard trap. Out-of-scope items were respected in spirit but not in letter: the ticket deferred the market-list category UI to a sibling ticket, and this PR does ship it (the filter rail replacing the dropdown). That expansion predates this run, is described in the PR body, and was approved by aganglada (5196621007); no new categories outside the market data schema were added. This run itself changed no acceptance-criterion behaviour — it addressed 10 review comments on correctness, performance and stale docs.
